claim: L1's mechanical `conditioned_scope_clause.is_unconditioned_subject` flag only inspects the text preceding the requirement's first RFC2119 keyword (the subject clause). It does NOT detect applicability-narrowing restrictions embedded later in the sentence, inside the verb phrase or object -- e.g. req-1-eip155-chainid's subject is bare 'Tested code' (flagged unconditioned=True), but the actual obligation is 'create hashes FOR TRANSACTIONS that incorporate chainid' -- 'for transactions' is a real restriction (this only applies to code that constructs off-chain-signable transaction-style hashes, e.g. EIP-712/meta-tx/permit signatures; a contract that never does this is NOT_APPLICABLE), just not captured by the mechanical subject-clause flag. Similarly req-2-overflow-underflow's bare 'Tested code' subject hides the real restriction 'contain calculations that CAN overflow or underflow' -- applicability requires arithmetic operations capable of overflow/underflow (largely relevant only to pre-0.8.0 code, `unchecked{}` blocks, or inline-assembly arithmetic, given Solidity >=0.8.0's default overflow checks), not literally all code.
why_unavoidable: Reliably distinguishing 'restriction in the subject clause' from 'restriction in the predicate/object' via pure regex/HTML-structure parsing (L1's approach) would require a much deeper syntactic (near-NLP) parse than the mechanical, auditable extraction the L1 parser is designed to do. Rather than build that speculative NLP layer now, this is logged as a required MANUAL RE-READ step at L3 for every requirement, not solved mechanically.
blast_radius: req-1-eip155-chainid L3 applicability_rule
req-2-overflow-underflow L3 applicability_rule
any future Track B requirement whose is_unconditioned_subject=True must be manually re-read for predicate-embedded restrictions before its L3 applicability_rule is trusted

claim: The L6 trigger component description for req-2-verify-exact-balance-check ('trigger-exact-balance-eq') extends the detectable pattern to 'an `==`/`!=` comparison where one operand is ... a call to a balanceOf-shaped function' -- but the requirement's own text says only 'the balance of an account', which directly and unambiguously names native ETH balance (Solidity's `.balance` member, matching the sibling S requirement req-1-exact-balance-check's own wording). Generalizing to ERC20-style `balanceOf()` token balances is importing an external Solidity/token-standard convention not stated in EthTrust's text -- caught during a self-review pass for this go/no-go check, not by the original L6 authoring.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- this is a correctable overreach, not a genuine textual gap. Logged here rather than silently narrowed, per the register's purpose of surfacing exactly this kind of creeping generalization before it goes unnoticed into Track B.
blast_radius: rtf/track_a/l6_level_m_extraction/req-2-verify-exact-balance-check.json's trigger-exact-balance-eq component note
resolution: Corrected in the same pass: trigger-exact-balance-eq's note narrowed to '.balance'-style native-ETH comparisons only, matching req-1-exact-balance-check's own wording. No textual basis for including token balanceOf() was found elsewhere in the spec.

claim: The independent-reviewer subagent classified pooltogether/H-02 (a uint256-to-uint96 narrowing downcast in Vault._burn that silently truncates share amounts) as DIRECT evidence for req-2-overflow-underflow ('calculations that can overflow or underflow'). Verified against the actual finding text (confirmed fix: 'Added SafeCast') and found this conflates two distinct failure classes: a narrowing TYPE CAST that truncates a value (no arithmetic operation involved, nothing 'calculates' anything) versus an arithmetic CALCULATION whose result exceeds/goes below its type's representable range. Corrected to CONTEXTUAL in rtf/l11_correspondence/correspondence_mapping.json.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- corrected on manual verification. Logged because this is exactly the kind of plausible-sounding-but-technically-wrong conflation an independent reviewer (human or model) can make when working at speed across many findings, and because 9 of the same reviewer's other 9 req-2-overflow-underflow classifications were checked and found genuinely well-grounded (real arithmetic operations, real underflow/overflow mechanisms cited with specific code) -- this was not a systemic failure of the correspondence-building process, but it does mean 'independent review' alone, without a verification pass by whoever consumes the mapping, is not sufficient quality assurance on its own.
blast_radius: rtf/l11_correspondence/correspondence_mapping.json's one corrected record
any future L12 evaluation using this correspondence mapping for recall metrics -- the DIRECT-mapping count for req-2-overflow-underflow drops from 10 to 9 as a result
resolution: Corrected in place in correspondence_mapping.json; review_status field on that record updated to 'corrected_on_manual_verification_by_orchestrating_session' rather than silently overwritten with no trace.

req_id_or_section: L1 corpus-wide parser (surfaced via req-2-documented, req-2-self-destruct, req-2-external-calls, req-2-check-rounding, req-2-safe-assembly, req-2-protect-create2, req-2-malleable-signatures-for-replay -- 7 requirements found during Track B M-level work)
claim: L1's `extend_until_modality` sibling-block-gluing logic only activates when the header paragraph has NO RFC2119 keyword at all. Several requirements have their RFC2119 keyword INSIDE the header (e.g. 'Tested Code MUST document the need for each instance of:'), immediately followed by a colon introducing a <ul> that is essential to the requirement's actual content (in req-2-documented's case, 8 specifically named trigger constructs) -- but because a MUST is already found in the header, the gluing rule never fires, so `normative_text` silently truncates at the colon, and this truncation propagates into every L2 context bundle's `self` field (which reads directly from `normative_text`). Not caught during Phase 0/1 development because none of the 6 Track A requirements happened to have this shape; found only once Track B's broader M-level sweep hit real examples.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- a real, fixable parser gap (the same fix pattern already built for the no-keyword-at-all case generalizes: also glue a following <ul> when the header ends in ':' regardless of whether a keyword was already found). Not yet fixed in rtf/l1_corpus/parse_spec.py as of this entry -- the 7 affected requirements' true full text was extracted by hand (direct raw HTML read) for this Track B M-level analysis pass, bypassing the truncated L1/L2 fields for just these 7, rather than blocking on a parser fix mid-batch.
blast_radius: rtf/l1_corpus/requirement_corpus.json's normative_text field for these 7 requirements (and any others sharing this colon-terminated-header shape not yet enumerated -- a full corpus sweep for this pattern has not been done)
rtf/l2_context_bundles/*.json's 'self' field for the same 7+ requirements, since it reads normative_text directly
any future L3+ work on these requirements MUST re-verify against raw HTML rather than trusting the L1/L2 fields at face value until the parser is fixed and re-run
resolution: Fixed in rtf/l1_corpus/parse_spec.py (_looks_incomplete() generalizes the extension trigger to colon-terminated headers and dangling-keyword cases), full corpus re-parsed and L2 bundles regenerated. Diff against the pre-fix corpus confirmed 7 requirements changed (all pure extensions, zero shortened), referential integrity held before and after. See PARSING_NOTES.md for the full writeup.

claim: The framework's PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE conformance schema (L8) was designed with MUST-level requirements in mind. 10 of 11 GP requirements use SHOULD, an explicitly non-binding, non-certification-blocking recommendation per RFC2119 convention and per EthTrust's own certification model (Level [S]/[M]/[Q] gates are built from MUST requirements; GP is a separate, advisory section). Whether a 'FAIL' on a SHOULD-level requirement should be reported identically to a 'FAIL' on a MUST-level one (same schema, same downstream metrics) or whether GP results need a distinguishable presentation (e.g. an 'ADVISORY_NOT_MET' state, or simply excluding GP from any pass/fail-rate metric entirely) was not resolved in this pass -- generated GP records using the same PASS/FAIL vocabulary as MUST-level requirements for consistency, but flagging this as a genuine, not-yet-decided design question rather than a silent choice.
why_unavoidable: A real open design question, not an error -- reusing the existing schema was the pragmatic choice to keep GP records in the same shape as the rest of the corpus for this pass, but the underlying question (does non-binding advisory conformance deserve a different formal state than binding conformance) deserves a real decision before any GP results are reported in evaluation metrics.
blast_radius: Any future L12 evaluation that includes GP requirements in aggregate pass/fail statistics without separating them from MUST-level results
rtf/track_a/l_gp_recommended_practice/*.json's use of the standard PASS/FAIL vocabulary

claim: find_create2_usage()'s assembly-shape branch (committed in an earlier L5 pass) checked `node.inline_asm` for the literal 'create2' substring on ASSEMBLY-type nodes. Direct inspection during req-2-protect-create2 implementation found that Slither's `node.inline_asm` (backed by `_asm_source_code`) is NOT populated for a stock 0.8.20 compile of a plain `assembly { ... }` block -- it returns None even when the block plainly contains `create2` -- so this branch was silently dead code: it could never fire, regardless of input. Not caught earlier because the original test_predicates.py::test_create2 only exercised the high-level `new X{salt:...}()` shape, never the assembly shape, so the always-None condition never surfaced as a test failure.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- a real, fixable predicate bug, found only because implementing req-2-protect-create2's own assembly-create2 evidence-gap case required exercising this code path with a real fixture for the first time.
blast_radius: find_create2_usage()'s assembly-detection branch for req-1-no-create2 -- any prior claim that this requirement's assembly-CREATE2 shape was covered was incorrect; only the high-level new{salt:} shape was ever actually detected

the new find_create2_deployed_target_violations() for req-2-protect-create2, which shares the same node-text-extraction technique and would have inherited the identical dead-code bug had it not been caught here first
resolution: Added `_assembly_block_text(node)` helper in rtf/l5_predicates/predicates.py, falling back to `node.source_mapping.content` (confirmed reliably populated) when `node.inline_asm` is empty. Both find_create2_usage() and find_create2_deployed_target_violations() switched to this helper. New test coverage added for the previously-untested assembly-create2 shape in both test_create2() and test_create2_deployed_target_violations(); full suite (67/67) passing after the fix.

claim: Slither exposes no variable-read/write IR at all for identifiers referenced only inside an `assembly {}` block (confirmed empirically: `node.variables_written`/`node.state_variables_written` are always empty for ASSEMBLY-type nodes, even for a simple `sstore(fp.slot, raw)` case), so req-2-safe-assembly's predicate is necessarily built as a text-level regex match against the assembly block's raw source (via `_assembly_block_text`), not an IR-level one -- a real, load-bearing tool limitation, not a design choice. Separately and more severely: Slither's own Yul parser (`slither/solc_parsing/yul/parse_yul.py`) CRASHES with `SlitherException: unresolved reference to identifier <x>.address` when analyzing `.selector`/`.address` assignment on a LOCAL variable of EXTERNAL function-pointer type inside assembly -- confirmed by direct compilation attempt. This is Solidity's own supported syntax for that variable shape (the compiler itself rejects `.slot` there, only `.selector`/`.address` are valid) -- so this specific sub-case of req-2-safe-assembly's 'arbitrary values ... assigned to variables of type function' clause cannot be analyzed by Slither AT ALL, not even to the point of producing a compiled Slither object to run a predicate against.
why_unavoidable: A genuine upstream tool limitation (Slither's Yul parser does not support this valid Solidity construct), not a predicate design gap -- no predicate, however written, can run against a compilation that Slither itself cannot complete.
blast_radius: find_unsafe_assembly_variable_write()'s coverage of req-2-safe-assembly's function-typed-variable attack surface is necessarily partial: covers state-variable .slot-based writes (via sstore/`.slot :=`) but structurally cannot cover local external-function-pointer .selector/.address assignment

any future Level-S/M predicate touching assembly-block variable access inherits the same 'no variable IR inside assembly' limitation and must use the same text-level fallback, not assume Slither IR is available

req_id_or_section: L12 execution orchestrator (all requirements evaluated against real, multi-file EVMbench targets)
claim: Foundry (`forge`) cannot be installed on this HPC node -- confirmed via a real `foundryup` install attempt, not assumed: the precompiled binaries require GLIBC >= 2.29, and this node's glibc is older (foundryup itself reported 'GLIBC_2.29 not found' for forge/cast/anvil/chisel). Slither's own crytic-compile, when the compilation target lives inside a directory tree containing a `foundry.toml` (true for essentially every real EVMbench audit target, since EVMbench's own audits are Foundry projects), unconditionally shells out to `forge config`/`forge build` for two SEPARATE reasons discovered by direct trial: (1) `_init_platform`'s own Foundry detection when no `compile_force_framework` override is given, AND (2) even WITH `compile_force_framework='solc'` correctly forcing the actual compile platform, crytic_compile.py's `__init__` still runs a SEPARATE 'try to auto-detect remappings/solc-version from the working directory's build framework' check whenever the CWD (not just the target) is inside a Foundry project -- this second check is NOT gated by `compile_force_framework` at all.
why_unavoidable: The GLIBC mismatch is a genuine, unavoidable environment constraint on this specific node -- not fixable without root/a newer OS image. The crytic-compile auto-detection behavior is real upstream tool behavior (confirmed by reading crytic_compile.py's source directly, not guessed), not a bug in this project's own code.
blast_radius: Any L12 orchestrator run against a real, multi-file EVMbench target (as opposed to this project's single-file synthetic test fixtures) needs the workaround in rtf/l5_predicates/compile_helper.py::compile_evmbench_target() -- setting cwd to a directory with no reachable foundry.toml, and supplying every import remapping (collected recursively across ALL nested lib/ dependencies' own remappings.txt files, not just the project's top-level one) as absolute paths explicitly, rather than relying on crytic-compile's normal Foundry-aware auto-configuration
resolution: Implemented rtf/l5_predicates/compile_helper.py::compile_evmbench_target() (+ _collect_remappings()), confirmed working end-to-end against the real 2023-07-pooltogether Vault.sol (36 real contracts compiled, including Vault, PrizePool, TwabController, and their full real dependency graph -- OpenZeppelin, prb-math, etc.), with zero forge invocation. One unrelated, separately-logged Slither IR-generation limitation surfaced on TierCalculationLib.getTierOdds during this same compile (a 'NoneType has no attribute parameters' internal error) -- a genuine Slither limitation on this specific function, not connected to the remapping/cwd workaround itself, and does not block compilation of the rest of the target.

claim: The first implementation of target_localization_accuracy() compared only the CONTRACT NAME prefix of a location string ('Vault' from 'Vault._burn'), not the full 'Contract.function' location -- a real bug, not caught by this module's own unit tests at the time, because the existing negative-case test happened to use a DIFFERENT contract name (masking the same-contract-different-function false-positive case entirely). Found by this project's own FIRST real evaluation run against 2023-07-pooltogether: it reported 2/2 (100%) target localization accuracy, but manual inspection of the raw evidence showed the H-02 finding's real ground-truth locations (Vault._mint/_burn/_transfer, extracted directly from the fix-patch diff) were never actually present in RTF's collected evidence for that requirement (find_unvalidated_function_parameters only scans public/external functions; _mint/_burn/_transfer are internal overrides) -- the metric was trivially matching on the shared contract name alone.
why_unavoidable: A genuine implementation defect in the metrics module itself, not a design tradeoff -- caught only by actually running a real evaluation against real ground truth with real (not synthetic) location data, exactly the kind of gap synthetic unit tests alone could not have revealed.
blast_radius: Any metric result computed with the pre-fix target_localization_accuracy() would have overstated localization precision for any target where multiple candidate locations share one contract/file -- true of essentially every real Solidity file with more than one function

The first frozen evaluation's manifest (frozen at git commit d4f7ba6) is stale relative to this fix and was re-frozen after -- see freeze_gate.py's refusal to silently overwrite a frozen manifest, which correctly required an explicit delete+re-freeze step for this fix
resolution: Fixed to compare the full lowercased location string (Contract.function), not just the contract-name prefix. New regression test added (test_target_localization_accuracy's same-contract-different-function case) specifically covering the shape of bug that let this through originally. Permitted post-evaluation change reason per the plan's policy: 'implementation defect' -- re-computed, not tuned to any observed benchmark score (the fix makes the metric MORE conservative/harsher, not more favorable).

claim: find_unvalidated_function_parameters() originally scanned only public/external functions. Re-derivation from the requirement's own normative text and definitions ('Tested Code MUST validate inputs...', with 'Tested Code' defined broadly as all of a contract's/related contracts' Solidity source, no visibility restriction anywhere) found NO textual basis for the public/external-only restriction -- it was an unexamined convention imported from general Solidity-audit attack-surface framing ("only the external interface matters"), never derived from this requirement's own text, and never logged as an assumption at the time it was introduced. This is judged a genuine IMPLEMENTATION DEFECT (incorrect requirement interpretation), not a defensible scoping choice -- confirmed concretely, not just in principle: on a real EVMbench target (2023-07-pooltogether), the pre-fix scope missed Vault._burn/_mint/_transfer entirely (internal overrides containing the exact uint96(_shares) truncating cast that IS EVMbench finding H-02, with zero require()/assert() touching _shares in any of the three), meaning RTF's L12 v1 run 1 evaluation's H-02 localization miss traces DIRECTLY to this defect, not to a genuine text-derivation limit.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- a real, now-fixed implementation bug. Investigated specifically at user request to determine whether H-02's miss reflected a defect vs. a genuine EthTrust-text limitation; conclusively the former.
blast_radius: find_unvalidated_function_parameters()'s prior evidence output for req-3-all-valid-inputs across any earlier run (including the archived v1 run 1) undercounted true unvalidated-input sites -- the archived run 1 record is NOT retroactively altered (immutable per archive_run.py's design) but is now known to be based on an under-scoped predicate

Fixed scope is also considerably noisier (flags many more internal helper functions, most not security-relevant) -- an expected, disclosed precision/recall tradeoff for a DETERMINISTIC_EVIDENCE_ONLY component, not treated as a new defect
resolution: find_unvalidated_function_parameters() now scans ALL functions regardless of visibility. New regression test (test_unvalidated_function_parameters_covers_internal_functions) reproduces the exact real-world shape (internal function, truncating cast, zero require/assert) and confirms detection. Verified directly against the real pooltogether target: Vault._burn/_mint/_transfer now all appear in the predicate's evidence output. Permitted post-evaluation change reason per the plan's policy: incorrect requirement interpretation -- not motivated by 'improves EVMbench performance' (the investigation was conducted using only the original EthTrust derivation, before checking what effect the fix would have on any score).

why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- a deliberate, logged version bump, exactly the kind of change the plan's post-evaluation change policy exists to make auditable rather than silent. claim: judge_result() reported the FIRST pass's raw decision as the requirement's final conformance_state even when judge_with_second_pass()'s own disagreement flag was False -- silently ignoring exactly the signal the plan's own mandatory-second-pass rule exists to surface (a PASS/FAIL the model itself couldn't reproduce on a second, independent attempt should not be trusted at face value). Found live, before the first official RTF v2 evaluation run was archived, while validating v2's enriched evidence against the real tempo-mpp-streams target: req-2-signature-verification's first pass said FAIL, but the raw second_pass_agreement was False, and the pre-fix code silently reported FAIL as final anyway.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- a real, now-fixed implementation gap in this session's own new L8-bridge code (judge_with_l8.py), not a pre-existing framework defect. Caught by actually running the full pipeline against real evidence, not by unit tests alone (the pure decision logic is now unit-tested via resolve_conformance_from_judgment(), but the ORIGINAL bug -- ignoring the agree flag entirely -- existed because no test had checked that specific interaction before this real run surfaced it).
blast_radius: Any RTF v1 run 2 second-pass-judged result (pooltogether/tempo-mpp-streams DIRECT requirements) that happened to have second_pass_agree=False was affected -- reviewed: run 2's own results (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on all 4, all agree=True) were NOT affected by this bug, since it only changes behavior when agree is explicitly False
Extracted into a new pure function resolve_conformance_from_judgment(), now directly unit-tested (4 new tests) without needing a live LLM call
resolution: judge_result() now calls resolve_conformance_from_judgment(decision, second_pass_agree), which downgrades to INCONCLUSIVE whenever second_pass_agree is False, regardless of what the first pass said. Re-froze RTF v2's manifest at the commit including this fix (still labeled 0.2.0-evidence-enrichment -- this is a correction to v2's own construction, found before v2's first official evaluation run, not a separate v3 change).

claim: Auditing the current LLM call configuration (Phase H work item 1) found two real, previously-unpinned fields: a4v.llm.ChatClient never sent top_p or max_tokens in its request body (only model/messages/temperature), meaning every prior RTF judgment call -- and every Commentator/Auditor call, since ChatClient is genuinely shared production infrastructure, confirmed via grep of every `from a4v.llm import`/`import a4v.llm` site -- silently used whatever provider/model default applied, invisibly and unrecorded. Fixed by adding top_p/max_tokens as new OPTIONAL parameters (default None) threaded through ChatClient._cache_key/_post/complete/complete_json: omitted from both the request body and the cache-key hash payload when None, so every existing caller that never passes them (Commentator, Auditor, existing tests) is byte-for-byte unaffected -- same request body, same cache-key hash, same on-disk cache entries as before this change. RTF's own LLMJudgmentLayer now pins top_p=1.0 (explicit no-op sampling pin, not a behavior change) and max_tokens=4096 (a procedural, not empirically-tuned, headroom choice) specifically for its own calls, via new constructor fields, without touching ChatClient's own defaults. Every judgment artifact now automatically carries a `judgment_config` block (provider, model_id, api_base_url, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, timeout_seconds, retry_max_attempts/wait_multiplier/wait_min/wait_max, prompt_version, schema_version, cache_key) plus a `schema_version` field -- both now required by schema.py's validate_judgment(), so a judgment missing this metadata fails validation rather than silently passing through incomplete.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- a real configuration-completeness gap, exactly what work item 1 asked to find and fix ('If any field is not currently pinned, fix that before running further experiments'). The max_tokens=4096 and top_p=1.0 values themselves are logged as procedural design choices here, not empirically validated against a truncation/quality case -- if a future stability/model-comparison experiment (work items 6-7) finds evidence these values are wrong (e.g. real truncation at 4096, or top_p!=1.0 mattering at temperature=0.0), that is grounds for a further, separately-logged change, not something already validated by this entry.
blast_radius: Every L8 judgment call made from this point forward has a materially different cache key than the equivalent pre-change call would have (since top_p/max_tokens are now part of the hashed payload whenever the caller -- i.e. LLMJudgmentLayer -- passes them) -- this is intentional: a cached response generated under different, unpinned sampling settings must not be silently served for a call now made under pinned settings

schema.py's REQUIRED_FIELDS grew two entries (schema_version, judgment_config) -- any judgment dict constructed by hand in a test fixture without these two keys now fails validate_judgment(); all in-repo test fixtures (selftest.py) were updated in this same pass

a4v/llm.py gained new exported constants (RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS, RETRY_WAIT_MULTIPLIER, RETRY_WAIT_MIN, RETRY_WAIT_MAX, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) and a stored self.timeout attribute on ChatClient -- purely additive, does not change any existing behavior or call signature default

claim: Tracing the evidence flow (Phase H work item 2) found and precisely root-caused the exact mechanism behind RTF_V2_RUN1_REPORT.md's PoolTogether evidence-dilution finding: build_judgment_question's flat evidence[:30] cutoff took the first 30 items in an order that is fully DETERMINISTIC but carries zero relevance signal (predicate-registration order x Slither's own internal contract-enumeration order). Counted directly against the real archived v2 run 1 artifact (not estimated): req-3-all-valid-inputs produced 739 raw items, 383 of which (52%) are find_unvalidated_function_parameters findings against `console2` -- forge-std's debug-logging shim, vendored transitively under lib/forge-std/, zero audit relevance -- which happens to sort first. Caught by this module's own real-data regression test failing, not assumed correct.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- a real, now-fixed evidence-serialization/prompt-construction defect (the flat cutoff), found by actually tracing the pipeline against real data per explicit user instruction, not by re-reading code in the abstract. The relative-path bug above is similarly a real implementation defect in this same session's own new code, caught by the new module's own test suite before being trusted.

claim: The Phase H live stability experiment (9 cases x 2 models, real API calls) initially showed EVERY case landing on INCONCLUSIVE/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE for openai/gpt-5.1-codex-max, including cases that should be unambiguous (a synthetic unsafe narrowing cast with zero validation) and a real case (PoolTogether Vault._burn's narrowing-cast evidence in isolation) that a prior live_validation run (Run 4, documented in RTF_V2_RUN1_REPORT.md) had already gotten a confident FAIL on with the SAME underlying evidence. First hypothesis (this session's own new max_tokens=4096 pin from work item 1) was tested directly via a 3-way A/B comparison (uncapped vs 4096 vs 16000, single calls, identical prompt) and CLEANLY RULED OUT -- all three gave FAIL/MEDIUM confidence with near-identical reasoning. Root cause found by reconstructing the EXACT prompt text build_ranked_judgment_question() actually sends (free, deterministic, no API cost) and comparing it side-by-side against the A/B test's prompt: build_evidence_bundles() was taking the contributing predicate's own concrete `risk` text (e.g. 'values above X are silently truncated by this cast rather than rejected' -- the single most informative, specific piece of evidence) and appending it to the bundle's `limitations` list under a 'predicate-assessed risk (not an exploit claim): ...' hedging prefix, while `possible_failure_mechanism` (the field meant to carry exactly this information) got only a generic, weaker templated sentence. This actively signals uncertainty about a finding's own concrete mechanism to the LLM. Confirmed as the cause, not merely inferred: after fixing (risk text now populates `possible_failure_mechanism` directly when a predicate provides it, no longer duplicated into `limitations`), a targeted single-call re-test on the IDENTICAL real Vault._burn evidence flipped cleanly back to FAIL/MEDIUM confidence.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- a real implementation defect in this same session's own new bundle-construction code (evidence_ranking.py, added earlier in this Phase H pass), found only by actually running the pipeline live and comparing its exact rendered output against a controlled alternative -- not visible from reading the code in isolation (the fields LOOKED individually reasonable; the bug was in which field the risk text ended up in, and the hedging language wrapped around it there specifically).

claim: The Phase H live stability experiment measured citation validity across all 18 (case, model) live calls as an explicit pre-registered acceptance metric (work item 6). Result: 0/12 valid for openai/gpt-5.1-codex-max, 0/19 valid for z-ai/glm-5.2 -- but investigation of the actual failure reasons shows this is NOT a model citation-quality problem. verify_evidence_citations()'s LOCATION_RE expects a file-path-like shape ("path/to/file.sol", optionally ":line" or "#Symbol"), consistent with judgment_layer.py's own system prompt instructions ("location": "path:line_or_symbol"). But RTF's OWN evidence rendering (both the pre-existing flat _render_evidence_line() and this session's new evidence_ranking.py bundle renderer) has, since this project's earliest predicates, always labeled evidence locations as "Contract.function" (e.g. "Vault._burn"), never a file path. Both models faithfully echoed the EXACT location string shown to them in the prompt ("Vault._burn") back into evidence[].location, which verify_evidence_citations() then treats as a literal, nonexistent file path ("file not found: .../checkout/vault/Vault._burn") and marks invalid, every single time, regardless of whether the underlying claim is accurate. This is a real, pre-existing internal inconsistency between RTF's evidence-location convention and its own citation-check's expected format -- not introduced this session, but only now measured directly because this is the first time citation validity was checked as an explicit metric across a live batch.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- a real, fixable design inconsistency, but genuinely out of scope to silently patch within this pass: closing it requires a real design decision (should predicates emit a resolvable file:line location alongside the existing Contract.function label; should citation_check learn to resolve Contract.function symbols via source mapping) that work items 1-9 did not ask for and that risks scope creep into re-architecting evidence location tracking mid-experiment.

claim: A dedicated root-cause investigation (13 pre-registered, single-variable live ablations, $0.18 spend) of the 4 GPT INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE outcomes among 7 known-expectation Phase H cases found THREE independent root causes, none of which is 'the LLM needs more context' or 'evidence dilution' taken generically. (1) Cases 2/4 (PASS-expected): a target-wide judgment QUESTION combined with location-scoped evidence -- logically, one clean local example cannot prove a universally-quantified requirement ('MUST validate ALL inputs', 'MUST PROPERLY verify signatures') holds target-wide, even though one bad example CAN disprove it. Confirmed causal: rewording ONLY the question's scope from target-wide to location-scoped flipped both cases cleanly to the correct answer (AB2, AB4); an explicit 'you may conclude PASS' permission sentence, tested as a competing hypothesis, did NOT flip either case (AB1, AB3), ruling out simple prompt-instruction wording as the driver. (2) Case 3 (FAIL-expected, unchecked ecrecover): the model's hedge was NOT resolved by adding literal source code (AB5) or by simplifying the requirement's wording (AB6), but WAS resolved -- to PASS, the OPPOSITE of the originally assumed correct answer -- once one explicit fact was supplied: that the value ecrecover's result is compared against (authorizedSigner) is confirmed non-zero and immutable (AB12). This revealed that this session's OWN synthetic test-case label ('expected: FAIL') was underspecified: find_unchecked_ecrecover_result proves a check is ABSENT (unconditional, local fact) but signature-verification's real risk is RELATIONAL (conditional on the comparator's own possible range), which no predicate currently establishes -- meaning the model's original caution was arguably the epistemically correct response to genuinely incomplete evidence, not a defect. (3) Case 8 (PoolTogether, FAIL-expected, 30 ranked bundles): the SAME top-ranked Vault._burn evidence that alone produces a confident FAIL (case 7) stops doing so once ~20+ other candidate bundles are also present in the prompt -- a real, volume-bounded effect (FAIL held through top-10, flipped by top-20) confirmed INDEPENDENT of cases 2/4's mechanism via a decisive test: applying the SAME location-scoped-question fix that resolved cases 2/4 to case 8 did NOT resolve it (AB13, a clean null result). The exact mechanism behind case 8's effect (raw volume vs. competing semantic claims vs. other) remains explicitly UNRESOLVED -- the discriminating experiments (token-matched neutral padding, finer-grained bisection) were not run in this pass and are logged as open follow-up, not guessed at.
why_unavoidable: Not unavoidable -- a real, structured diagnostic investigation performed at the user's explicit request, specifically to avoid jumping to an unverified 'more context fixes it' conclusion. The findings themselves (granularity mismatch, relational-evidence gap, volume-bounded interference) are genuine architectural/test-design discoveries, verified via controlled single-variable ablation rather than assumed.
